# troth

> A persistent AI partner whose mind lives outside the model. Identity, memory,
> goals and refusal walls persist in a local SQLite substrate (`~/.troth/state.db`)
> the operator owns; any LLM — Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi, a local model — is a
> swappable faculty on top. Swap the model, keep the mind. AGPL-3.0.

Runs on macOS and Linux, Node >= 22. Everything is local: no vendor account
holds any part of the partner, and engines fail over between each other.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): what troth is, install, the open/closed line
- [docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md](docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md): first-run setup — engines, keys, memory
- [docs/HONEST-LIMITS.md](docs/HONEST-LIMITS.md): the two properties the substrate does not claim to solve
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): release history, whole-product scope

## Run it

- `npm ci` then `node bin/troth.js setup` — guided setup (dashboard), or `--terminal` for the wizard
- `node bin/troth.js` — the chat REPL; `/help` lists every command
- `node bin/troth.js doctor` — what is configured, what is actually reachable
- `npm test` — the unit suite; `npm run journey` — out-of-process scenarios that
  drive the shipped surfaces (daemon wire protocol, CLI, HTTP API) on a throwaway HOME

## Agent setup (non-interactive)

An agent can configure troth without the wizard: write `~/.troth/config.json`
and verify with `node bin/troth.js doctor`. Minimal shapes — enable exactly one
to start, more later; troth fails over between enabled providers:

- Kimi Code membership: `{ "providers": { "kimi_sub": { "enabled": true, "apiKey": "<key>", "model": "k3" } } }`
- Anthropic API key:    `{ "providers": { "anthropic": { "enabled": true, "apiKey": "<key>" } } }`
- ChatGPT subscription: run `node bin/troth.js codex login` (device OAuth), then `{ "providers": { "openai_sub": { "enabled": true } } }`
- Claude Pro/Max:       run `node bin/troth.js install-plugin` — the plan answers inside Claude Code; no key in config
- Other keyed providers: `deepseek`, `openrouter`, `deepinfra`, `alibaba`, `moonshot`, `google_ai`, `xai`, `zai` — same `{ enabled, apiKey }` shape

Memory (embeddings + reranking) installs itself locally on first run; no
provider entry needed. Local CHAT models are optional and advanced — do not
configure one unless the operator asks. Secrets never echo: config is written
with owner-only permissions and the dashboard masks keys.

## Architecture

- [bin/troth-entity.js](bin/troth-entity.js): the entity daemon — one mind, JSON-lines wire protocol on stdio; faculties (engines) are wired here and dispatched per turn
- [shared-core/](shared-core/): the substrate — event-sourced state, classed memory (engrams), recall, dialogue window, transports for each engine
- [proxy/server.js](proxy/server.js): local HTTP proxy — dashboard UI, `/api/*` for setup, providers, memory import, local-model install
- [proxy/modules/router.js](proxy/modules/router.js): provider routing, fallback chains, the operator pin ("always use this engine")
- [plugin/](plugin/): the Claude Code plugin — slash commands, hooks and MCP servers that mount the substrate inside Claude Code
- [tests/journey/](tests/journey/): behaviour scenarios run against local, Docker Linux and the shipped DMG core; the release gate refuses a bundle that fails them

## Integration surfaces

- MCP: `plugin/mcp-servers/` — substrate, bash, cache, hashline, router servers, any MCP host can mount them ([docs/MCP-HOST-INSTALL.md](docs/MCP-HOST-INSTALL.md))
- HTTP: the proxy's `/api/*` (see `proxy/server.js`); Anthropic-compatible chat endpoint for tools that speak that shape
- Wire: the entity's stdin/stdout JSON-lines protocol (`user_input` in; `response`, `dispatch`, `serving` frames out)

- [benchmarks/](benchmarks/): reproducible harnesses for the properties the README claims
